# Emma's judgements — hand-recorded, never autogenerated

**Every row in this file is a verdict Emma gave in her own words.** Nothing here is inferred,
scored, or produced by a script, and nothing generated may be appended to it. That separation is
the point — Emma, 2026-08-25: *"keep these judgments on file in a file because these established
judgments can be built on lol like separate from anything autogenerated clearly from me lol."*

`reports/emma-judgments.tsv` is the same content machine-readable, one row per verdict, so a
matcher can be scored against it directly. The two are written together and must not drift.

Generated verdicts live elsewhere: `reports/multi-p2600-verdicts.tsv`,
`reports/multi-geni-parent-verdicts.tsv`, `reports/structural-walk-validation.tsv`. Those are
measurements. This is testimony, and it outranks them.

## How to use it

These are **the labelled set**. A rule proposed for the zipper join, the structural walk or any
future matcher is checked against this file first: if it disagrees with a row here, the rule is
wrong, not the row. New verdicts are appended as she gives them, with the date and her wording
where she gave any.

## The hard end, put to her the same day

She read sixteen easy rows in a row and said so: *"All of these seemed like easy ones lol I'm not
sure if you're only choosing ones you consider 'ambiguous'... I'm confused what a hard one will
even look like."* The sample was random and then **sorted easiest-first at her own instruction**,
so the ordering was the artefact, not the population.

`reports/zipper-evidence.tsv` measures the population instead of guessing at it — all 23,596
pairs, banded by how much a human would have to go on. **33.2% look like the sixteen** (both sides
name both parents and both agree). The hard tail is `NAMES-CONFLICT` at **3.2%** and `NO-PARENTS`
at **10.3%**. Four of those went to her:

| # | round | ours | theirs | verdict |
| ---: | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| 17 | 1 | Sigrid Charlotta Fleming af Liebelitz `386743189540005666` | `Q4959104` Hedvig Charlotta Klinckowström | **Wrong — drop it** |
| 18 | 1 | Lars Bengtsson Hierta `4240537919610035130` | `Q110386205` Laurens Bentsån 'Griis' | **Right** |
| 19 | 1 | Margareta Gödiksdotter Fincke `4085368611040124960` | `Q105796231` Marjatta of Porkkala | **Right** |
| 20 | 1 | Eleonora Juliana Wiggman `342026151920011851` | `Q29246906` Eleonora von Sydow | **Right** |

Her wording on the two she would not call:

- **8, John de Mohun** — *"Need pages opened, imo this should be adder to the queue as a web
  browser based project of yours at the end to do the resolution because this is thorny."* Both
  parents match by name (John de Mohun / Joan de Ferrers) and the generations repeat those names,
  so a name match cannot separate father from son.
- **11, Brita Gustafsdotter Bååt** — *"Can't tell."* Father matches; the mothers are both Görvel
  but one is `Gyllenhorn` and one is `Joensdotter av Hacksta`.

Her wording on **15**, which is a finding rather than a verdict:

> *"Both right but importantly we found something. Wikidata mother should have NN overwritten with
> geni name and identified with."*

Their `P25` mother on `Q6188549` is the literal placeholder **`NN`**. Ours is
**Carin Pedersdotter Fargalt**. So the merge is right *and* it exposes a whole class of edit —
see § *What came out of it* below.

## What came out of it — rules, in her judgements' own terms

These are read off the sixteen, not asserted in advance. Each one is falsifiable by a later row.

**A name that differs is not a parent that differs.** Every one of the fourteen `Right` verdicts
survived at least one parent name that does not match as a string, and she called them right
anyway. The variation she accepted, by kind:

| kind | example | rows |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| spelling / language | `Diderich`/`Diderik`, `Gustaf`/`Gustav`, `Itta di Spoleto`/`Itta of Spoleto` | 2, 11, 14 |
| title added or dropped | `Jean de Forez` / `Jean I Comte de Forez` | 9 |
| occupation added | `Diderich Brodersen` / `pastor Diderik Brodersen` | 14 |
| family name vs territory | `de La Tour du Pin` / `de Viennois`; `Uta von Tengling-Peilstein und Kleeberg` / `Uta von Peilstein` | 7, 9 |
| patronymic vs territory | `Sophie Valdemarsdatter` / `Sophie of Denmark` | 10 |
| family name shift in one lifetime | `Ulyanin` / `Ulyanov` | 12 |

**An absent parent on their side is not a disagreement.** Rows 12, 13, 14 and 16 all have a
`-` in a Wikidata parent slot and were called Right. Row 16 has *no parents at all on our side* and
was still Right. This is the same rule `CLAUDE.md` states for absence generally and the same one
that renamed `CONTRADICTED` to `PARENTS-NOT-JOINED`: **absence never refutes.**

**An `NN` on their side is an absence, not a name.** Row 15. It is also an opportunity — see below.

**A pair with no evidence at all is still acceptable to her.** Row 20 has no parents on either
side, a given name that matches and a surname that does not, and she called it **Right**. So
`NO-PARENTS` — 10.3% of the join — is not a band to strip out, and the third option offered
("a pair with no corroboration should not be in the correspondence at all") was declined. Position
is evidence in her model even when nothing else is.

**The one Wrong is a whole different shape, and it is nameable.** Row 17 is the only pair of the
twenty where the person's *own* name shares no word with theirs **and** all four parents are
different people. Rows 18 and 19 also have own-names that share no word — `Lars`/`Laurens`,
`Margareta`/`Marjatta` — and she called both Right, because their parents are the same people in
another orthography. So the discriminator is not "the names differ". It is **whether the parents
resolve to the same people once language is allowed for.**

**Orthography and language are not evidence of difference, at all.** Row 18 is Swedish against a
Danish-Latin rendering (`Bengt`→`Benedikt`, `Torkel`→`Thorgils`) and row 19 is Swedish against
Finnish (`Gustafsson`→`Kustaanpoika`, `Nilsdotter`→`Niilontytär`). Both Right. Together with the
sixteen this means **every kind of name variation put to her has been accepted**, and the only
rejection turned on the people, not the strings.

**Round number did not predict error in this sample.** Three of the sixteen are round 3 and all
three were Right; both browser referrals are rounds 2 and 3. The `ROUND_CAP = 3` in
`scripts/zipper-join.py` is untouched by this — sixteen rows cannot move a cap set against a
date-measured error curve — but nothing here argues for lowering it.

**Where she stopped is where the family repeats a name across generations.** Row 8 is a John son
of a John, and row 11 is one of two Görvels. That is the shape to route to the browser: not "the
names differ" but **"the names match and there is more than one candidate they could match."**

## Open items this produced

- **Browser resolution project** — rows 8 and 11, and everything shaped like them.
  `queue.md` § *Browser-based resolution of thorny merges*.
- **Drop `386743189540005666` ↔ `Q4959104`** from the correspondence — the one Wrong. It needs a
  refutation file the way `structural-walk-validation.tsv` refutes the structural walk, so that a
  re-run of `zipper-join.py` does not simply propose it again.
- **`NN` mothers on Wikidata** — row 15. Where our tree names a parent and Wikidata's `P22`/`P25`
  points at an item whose label is the placeholder `NN`, that item can be **given the Geni name and
  identified**. Nothing measures how many of these there are yet.
